newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF sale by private auction - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF sale by private auction - paper.

text.p: The French government is planning to sell Thomson-CSF through a private auction to the highest bidder among a group of selected industrial candidates, financial daily Les Echos reported on Tuesday.

The new procedure would make price the determining factor in the privatisation process, over and above other considerations like industrial coherence which influenced the earlier sale process, the paper reported, citing unidentified sources.
The auction would only be open to "qualified" bidders based on their ideas for the future of the company and a list of terms and conditions imposed by the government, the paper reported.
Les Echos said the government used the current share price of Thomson-CSF to set a minimum price of 21 billion francs.
The decision would rule out a public share offering, the solution favoured by Thomson's managers and French Industry Minister Franck Borotra, the paper said.
The government originally said last October it would sell Thomson-CSF parent Thomson SA to French conglomerate Lagardere for the symbolic sum of one franc.
Under the plan, Lagardere was to sell heavily-indebted Thomson unit Thomson Multimedia to Korean firm Daewoo Electronics.
But the government suspended the sale process on December 4 after an independent privatisation commission refused to approve the terms. It particularly objected to Daewoo's involvement.
The paper did not say whether the government had made any decisions regarding a new plan to sell Thomson Multimedia.
Les Echos said that both Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom, the other bidder in the original process, were ready to make offers for Thomson-CSF under the new process.
